items.descriptionOriginal: Most of us routinely discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables at mealtime. But new research from King's College London suggests these scraps could be a valuable—and overlooked—source of dietary fiber, offering potential benefits for both public health and the environment.

items.title: Οι Millennials ανησυχούν όλο και περισσότερο για το ότι οι γονείς τους Boomer είναι κολλημένοι στα τηλέφωνά τους
items.titleOriginal: Millennials are growing concerned about their Boomer parents being glued to their phones
items.description: Οι Millennials δεν απέφευγαν ποτέ να μοιραστούν τα συναισθήματά τους για τους Boomer γονείς τους (και τις ικανότητες των παππούδων τους) στο Διαδίκτυο. Οι Millennials ενώνονται για άλλη μια φορά για να συζητήσουν μια παρόμοια παρατήρηση σχετικά με την απογοητευτική χρήση τηλεφώνου από τους γονείς τους Boomer. Σε ένα νήμα του Ιουλίου 2025 σχετικά με τις διαφορές γενεών στο subreddit r/generationology…
items.descriptionOriginal: Millennials have never shied away from sharing their feelings about their Boomer parents (and their grandparenting abilities ) on the Internet. Millennials are once again uniting to discuss a similar observation about their Boomer parents’ frustrating phone use. In a July 2025 thread about generational differences on the r/generationology subreddit, Millennial member Old-Beautiful-3971 shared their frustrating experience with their Boomer parents who are perpetually on their phones. “My parents are on the very young end of being ‘boomers’. For some reason they’re both acting like me when I was 20… that is to say, gluuuued to their phones,” they wrote. “I tried to have an important conversation with my dad this morning and he did not once look up (and I’m certain he was scrolling through Instagram videos).” An older man using a cellphone. Photo credit: Canva They went on to add, “The only difference is that when I was 20 he could, and would often say ‘Look at me when I’m talking to you. Put that thing away.’ But if I said that to him now he’d get defensive and probably yell at me for being disrespectful. What the heck???” Fellow Millennials agreed The passionate post got a rousing response from fellow Millennials who have experienced the same thing with their Boomer parents. “I have noticed it too and it makes me feel even weirder for having developed in the habit of flipping my phone face-down with my hands folded on top of it to let the person know that I’m listening for that they have my attention,” one commented. “And to think that it’s coming from the generation that tells everybody else that phones and TV will rot your brains.” Another shared, “My parents are visiting me right now. My dad is glued to his phone, even at the table during meals. Never once participating in the conversation except to point at the salt. This is the same man who would have screamed at me for bringing a book to the dinner table.” Others could commiserate about the role-reversal. “I’ve noticed this with my parents. It seems like I’ve switched places with them. I’m trying to use the online world less where as they are using it more and more,” one commented. A man looking pensive with phone in hand. Photo credit: Canva When phones take over family time Some Millennials noted that their Boomer parents’ phone use has impacted other activities they attempt to do together. “It’s become so difficult to watch a movie with my parents. I tell them to put away their phone. Sometimes movies take two days to finish,” another shared. Many Millennials also shared how they communicate with their parents when they notice it. “I am witnessing that as well, my boomer mom and my almost gen z brother visit and they are both glued to their phones. I try and ask if they can put them away because I don’t like my little son to see people like that. I do scroll but never when I am with him,” one Millennial shared. Researchers have a name for this: “phubbing,” or phone snubbing, which a 2016 study linked to lower relationship satisfaction among romantic partners. A related term, “technoference,” describes how parents’ device use interrupts family time, and research on parents has tied it to more behavior problems in children over time. Another added, “I stopped visiting my boomer mom for awhile. I told her to her face that I couldn’t stand the fact that I took the time to drive to her, which I really hate driving, it scares me and I’m not very good at it, and spend MY time with her only for her to be on her phone most of that time. I stopped calling her too because of all the times she’d put me on hold to take another call and then tell me that she’d have to call me back, but she never did. I still rarely call her. I just text so it’s less intrusive and hurtful for me. Now when I visit, her and her husband stay off their phones. They turn the TV down and only put quiet music on instead of blaring whatever crap they were watching. I did thank them for it.” Gen X isn’t off the hook either However, a Gen Z commenter was quick to point out that Gen X is guilty of the same habit. “My gen x parents are hella addicted to their phones (I’m 22 for context),” they wrote. “I’m not saying i’m not, but it’s really hypocritical when they’ll be bitching at me about ‘playing on my phone too much’ when they’re literal ipad kids lol. the reality is, screens and social media are addicting to ANYONE, regardless of age.” Other Millennials pointed out that it’s not just certain generations that are addicted to their phones. “I’m guilty of it as well. Everyone is at risk of screen addiction in this era,” another noted. And another Millennial quipped, “Phones are addictive, that doesn’t just like go away with oldness.” The data suggests they have a point: Pew Research Center’s 2025 survey found that 63% of adults ages 18 to 29 say they use the internet “almost constantly,” compared with 33% of those ages 50 to 64 and 14% of those 65 and older, even though 90% of adults 50 to 64 now own a smartphone. What’s with Boomers and their phones lately? by u/Old-Beautiful-3971 in generationology Phones are tough on every generation If there’s a takeaway from this thread, it’s that the phone gap is smaller than it feels. Millennials remember being told to put the screen away, and now some are watching their parents do the very thing they were scolded for. But as plenty of commenters pointed out, nobody is immune. Whether you’re 22 or 62, a phone is built to hold your attention. Maybe the real fix isn’t pointing fingers across generations, but doing what the commenter with the quiet TV and the put-away phones did: just say something, and see what happens. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Millennials are growing concerned about their Boomer parents being glued to their phones appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Μια μελέτη παρακολούθησε «χαρισματικά» παιδιά για περισσότερα από 50 χρόνια. Εδώ είναι τι μάθαμε για αυτούς.
items.titleOriginal: A study followed ‘gifted’ kids for over 50 years. Here’s what we’ve learned about them.
items.description: Στη δεκαετία του 1960, ο ψυχολόγος Julian Stanley συνειδητοποίησε ότι αν έπαιρνες τους καλύτερους μαθητές της έβδομης τάξης από όλη τη χώρα και τους έδινες τυπικές εισαγωγικές εξετάσεις, αυτά τα παιδιά θα βαθμολογούσαν, κατά μέσο όρο, περίπου όσο και ο τυπικός τελειόφοιτος του λυκείου. Ωστόσο, οι μαθητές της έβδομης τάξης που σημείωσαν εξίσου καλά ή καλύτερα από τους μαθητές του Λυκείου, ο Στα…
items.descriptionOriginal: In the 1960s, psychologist Julian Stanley realized that if you took the best-testing seventh graders from around the country and gave them standard college entry exams, those kids would score, on average, about as well as the typical college-bound high school senior. However, the seventh graders who scored as well or better than high schoolers, Stanley found, had off-the-charts aptitude in quantitative, logical, and spatial reasoning . In other words, they were gifted . In the 1970s, Stanley and his team launched a full-scale study , identifying many of America’s gifted kids and tracking them throughout their lives. The study, called the Study of Mathematically Precocious Youth (SMPY), never ended and is now more than 50 years in the making. It has followed more than 5,000 kids from middle school into adulthood. The study’s first two groups of participants, about 1,650 people, were identified as being in the top 1% of mathematical reasoning ability. When researchers checked in on them four decades later , 4.1% had earned tenure at a major research university, 2.3% were top executives at name-brand or Fortune 500 companies, and together they had secured 681 patents. Needless to say, a lot has changed with how students are today compared to 50 years ago. Stanley died in 2005, but the study continues at Vanderbilt University, where psychologist David Lubinski helped bring it in 1998. Lubinski, now a professor emeritus, and Camilla P. Benbow, dean of Vanderbilt’s Peabody College, still co-direct it. Why this study matters so much It’s not a stretch to call this one of the biggest and longest-running studies on intellectual “precociousness.” The results of the study thus far are both fascinating and genuinely surprising, a deeply insightful look into the minds and lives of brilliant children. 1. Some of what we used to think about gifted kids turned out to be wrong Ever heard the saying “early ripe, early rot”? It basically means doing “too much” to foster a kid’s special talents and abilities at too young an age could actually cause harm in the long term. That’s not even remotely true, at least not according to Lubinski. A 35-year SMPY study published in 2020 found that skipping grades and other forms of academic acceleration had no negative long-term effects on gifted kids’ psychological well-being at age 50. That saying might be an outdated example, but Lubinski says there are plenty of other misconceptions still alive today, like the idea that gifted kids are so smart that they’ll “find a way” to excel even if those smarts aren’t nurtured and developed. Not so fast. “They’re kids,” he explains. “They need guidance. We all need guidance.” 2. Intelligence is not the same as passion Quick, what’s the “smartest” career you can think of? Doctor? Scientist? While you do have to be pretty brilliant to work in medicine or science, those are far from the only career paths gifted kids choose later in life. “Quantitatively, gifted people vary widely in their passions,” Lubinski says. Many of the students in the study did end up pursuing medicine, but others went into fields like economics or engineering. Others still were more gifted in areas like logical or verbal reasoning, making them excellent lawyers and writers. “There are all kinds of ways to express intellectual talent,” Lubinski explains. When it comes to doing what’s best for a gifted student, it’s just as important for parents and educators to know what the student is passionate about rather than pigeonholing them in traditionally “smart” fields and registering them in a bunch of STEM courses. Students taking a test. Photo credit: Canva 3. Hard work definitely still matters Measuring a student’s aptitude, their natural abilities, is only one part of the equation when it comes to determining how successful they’ll be in life. Aptitude scores can identify a particularly strong natural skill set but tell us very little about how hard that person might work to excel in that field. Effort, Lubinski says, is a critical factor in determining how far someone will go in life. “If you look at exceptional performers in politics, science, music, and literature, they’re working many, many hours,” he says. (And for the record, there are a lot more important things in life than just career achievement, like family, friends, and overall happiness.) The idea that hard work still matters echoes the “10,000-hour rule,” popularized by journalist Malcolm Gladwell in his book Outliers: The Story of Success . Gladwell argued that people like Bill Gates and The Beatles excelled in part because they put in roughly 10,000 hours of practice. The psychologist whose research inspired the idea, Anders Ericsson, has said Gladwell oversimplified it: what matters is deliberate practice, not a magic number of hours. Students around a computer. Photo credit: Canva 4. Regardless of aptitude, every kid deserves to be treated as though they were gifted The study’s focus is specifically on kids within a certain range of intellectual ability, but Lubinski is careful to note that many of its findings can and should be applied to all students. For example, the children in the study who were allowed to take more challenging courses aligned with their skills and interests ultimately achieved more than those who were not afforded the same opportunity. “You have to find out where your child’s development is, how fast they learn, what are their strengths and relative weaknesses and tailor the curriculum accordingly,” Lubinski says. “It’s what you would want for all kids.” What this means for all kids It may sound a bit like a pipe dream, but it’s a great starting point for how we should be thinking about the future of education in America. After all, the SMPY data doesn’t just tell us something about the kids who tested in the top 1%. It tells us something universal: potential rarely announces itself fully formed. It has to be noticed, challenged, and given room to grow, whether that’s a math prodigy who needs to skip ahead a few grades or a kid with a quieter talent that doesn’t show up on any standardized test at all. Fifty years of tracking some of the most capable people in the country boils down to a pretty simple idea. Pay attention to what a kid is actually good at and actually loves, then get out of the way and let them run with it. This article originally appeared nine years ago. It has been updated. The post A study followed ‘gifted’ kids for over 50 years. Here’s what we’ve learned about them. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Χιλιάδες θεατές συναυλιών στην Πολωνία τραγουδούν αυθόρμητα το «Bohemian Rhapsody» και είναι άψογο
items.titleOriginal: Thousands of concertgoers in Poland spontaneously sing ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ and it’s flawless
items.description: Η μουσική των Queen έχει μια βαθιά σπλαχνική επίδραση σε τόσους πολλούς ανθρώπους. Λίγα έργα τέχνης μπορούν να κάνουν τους εντελώς άγνωστους να παραμερίσουν τις διαφορές τους και να ενωθούν στο τραγούδι, αλλά κατά τον Γκόλλυ, το “Bohemian Rhapsody” είναι ένα από αυτά. Θα ήταν ασαφές αν δεν ήταν τόσο όμορφο. Αυτό ισχύει ακόμη και σε χώρες όπου τα Αγγλικά δεν είναι η πρώτη λέξη…
items.descriptionOriginal: The music of Queen has a profound visceral effect on so many people. Few pieces of art can cause complete strangers to put aside their differences and come together in song, but by golly, “ Bohemian Rhapsody ” is one of them. It would be cheesy if it weren’t so absolutely beautiful. This holds true even in countries where English isn’t the first language, it appears. At Harry Styles’ July 2, 2023 concert in Warsaw, Poland, thousands of concertgoers began cheering as those iconic beginning piano notes penetrated the air. It happened before Harry even took the stage It wasn’t long before the entire stadium was singing along to that beloved tune and acing every single lyric. As one person commented on YouTube, “they sing Queen,” even though English isn’t Poland’s first language. (Poland actually ranks among the top 15 countries for English skills in EF’s English Proficiency Index , but the song’s pull clearly goes beyond language.) The passionate impromptu performance serves as a reminder of how special both Queen and the late Freddie Mercury remain today . “ No other band will ever come close to Queen . They were lightning in a bottle and Freddie was a whale in a teardrop. Once people keep singing his words, FM will live on forever,” another YouTube viewer wrote. Indeed, seeing an entire stadium come alive with “Bohemian Rhapsody,” you can’t help but feel Mercury’s soul return to the mortal plane, as if we’ve all been transported back to that historic Live Aid concert in 1985 when he had the entirety of Wembley Stadium wrapped around his finger for 21 glorious minutes. And then it happened again in Paris Just when you think nothing could top that, in July 2025, pianist Julien Cohen and about 30 pro-level musicians and singers came out of nowhere onto the streets of Paris to pull off an epic flash mob performance of the beloved hit, timed to the song’s 50th anniversary: That’s the true timeless beauty of this song. no matter who is singing it, it’s always a semi-spiritual experience that brings people together in a magical way. This article originally appeared three years ago. It has been updated. The post Thousands of concertgoers in Poland spontaneously sing ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ and it’s flawless appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: Her groundbreaking theory on the origin of life was rejected 15 times. Then biology proved her right.
items.description: Σε όλη τη γόνιμη και διακεκριμένη σταδιοδρομία της, η βιολόγος Lynn Margulis έκανε αρκετές πρωτοποριακές συνεισφορές στην επιστήμη που θεωρούμε δεδομένες ως κοινή γνώση σήμερα. Για παράδειγμα, υποστήριξε την «έννοια της Γαίας» του Τζέιμς Ε. Λάβλοκ, η οποία υποστήριξε ότι η Γη αυτορυθμίζεται για να διατηρεί συνθήκες ζωής. Αλλά με διαφορά, το πιο αξιοσημείωτο της…
items.descriptionOriginal: Throughout her prolific and distinguished career, biologist Lynn Margulis made several groundbreaking contributions to science that we take for granted as common knowledge today . For example, she championed James E. Lovelock’s “ Gaia concept ,” which posited that the Earth self-regulates to maintain conditions for life. But by far, her most notable theory was symbiogenesis. While it was first written off as “strange” and “aesthetically pleasing” but “not compelling,” it would ultimately prevail, and completely rewrite how we viewed the origin of life itself . The paper that changed everything In the late 1960s, Margulis wrote a paper titled “ On the Origin of Mitosing Cells ,” that was quite avant-garde. InThroughout her prolific and distinguished career, biologist Lynn Margulis (1938-2011) made several groundbreaking contributions to science that we take for granted as common knowledge today . For example, she helped develop James E. Lovelock’s “Gaia concept,” which posited that Earth’s living and nonliving systems form a self-regulating system that maintains conditions for life. But by far, her most notable theory was symbiogenesis. While it met plenty of skepticism, including a 1972 Science paper that called the symbiotic theory “aesthetically pleasing” but “not compelling,” it would ultimately prevail, and completely rewrite how we viewed the origin of life itself. The paper that changed everything In 1967, Margulis, then publishing under the name Lynn Sagan, wrote a paper titled “ On the Origin of Mitosing Cells ,” that was quite avant-garde. In it, she proposed a theory: that life evolved through organisms merging together to become inseparable. In essence, she argued that cooperation, not just competition, drives some of life’s biggest leaps. This challenged the neo-Darwinian emphasis on competition and gradual mutation that dominated scientific circles, though it didn’t overturn natural selection. Margulis’ paper was rejected by fifteen journals before getting accepted into the Journal of Theoretical Biology . By the late ’70s and early ’80s, research confirmed that mitochondria (found in plant and animal cells) and chloroplasts (found in plants and algae) were at one time independent bacteria. This showed that cooperation between organisms helped build the machinery inside our cells. And now that fact is written in textbooks, with no real story of the adversity it overcame to get there. The idea is still producing discoveries: in 2024, researchers reported the nitroplast , the first known nitrogen-fixing organelle, which appears to have evolved from a bacterium living inside a marine alga. How sexism nearly buried her work While it is customary for most new scientific theories to be met with criticism, especially those that completely shift the current narrative, many have noted that sexism played a key part in Margulis’ initial lack of acceptance. On more than one occasion, she herself had hinted that women were seen as mothers and wives first, and scientists second. Margulis, who was once married to fellow scientist Carl Sagan, told The University of Chicago Magazine in 2004, “I quit my job as a wife twice. It’s not humanly possible to be a good wife, a good mother, and a first-class scientist.” View this post on Instagram Her most controversial beliefs And yet, Margulis also held other controversial ideas that had nothing to do with her gender. Most famously, she did not believe that AIDS was caused by HIV, and instead believed it was caused by a syphilis-causing type of bacteria, despite there already being decades of research proving otherwise. That view was seen as an endorsement of AIDS denialism, which undermined prevention and treatment efforts. Then later in life, Margulis became a vocal proponent of 9/11 conspiracy theories suggesting government involvement in the Twin Towers attacks. And yet, perhaps this is one of those “you gotta take the good with the bad” situations. Margulis’ contrarian streak may have fueled both these unfounded, even harmful stances and the paradigm-shifting ideas that altered our understanding of life itself. View this post on Instagram And if nothing else, her story shows why science needs both open minds willing to challenge the consensus and rigorous evidence to test every claim. It seems life is, after all, about coming together. This article originally appeared in February. items.descriptionOriginal: Με τον Γιώργο Κούτσια να αναλαμβάνει πρωταγωνιστικό ρόλο σκοράροντας δύο φορές, η Φαμαλικάο πανηγύρισε μια σπουδαία πρόκριση στα ημιτελικά του League Cup Πορτογαλίας, αποκλείοντας την Μπράγκα στη διαδικασία των πέναλτι (3-1), έπειτα από ένα συγκλονιστικό παιχνίδι που ολοκληρώθηκε με σκορ 2-2 στην κανονική διάρκεια. Ο Έλληνας επιθετικός ήταν ο μεγάλος πρωταγωνιστής για την ομάδα του, καθώς βρήκε δύο φορές τον δρόμο προς τα δίχτυα μέσα στο πρώτο ημίχρονο, δίνοντας σημαντικό προβάδισμα στη Φαμαλικάο. Στο 16ο λεπτό, ο 22χρονος φορ άνοιξε το σκορ με εξαιρετικό σουτ στην κίνηση, αξιοποιώντας την ασίστ του Μάρκος Πένια και επιβεβαιώνοντας την πολύ καλή κατάσταση στην οποία βρίσκεται. Η Μπράγκα αντέδρασε και έφερε το ματς στα ίσα στο 37’, με τον Ρικάρντο Όρτα, ωστόσο ο Κούτσιας είχε ξανά την απάντηση. Στις καθυστερήσεις του πρώτου μέρους, η Φαμαλικάο κέρδισε πέναλτι και ο Έλληνας επιθετικός ανέλαβε την εκτέλεση, ευστοχώντας για το 2-1 και πετυχαίνοντας το δεύτερο προσωπικό του γκολ στην αναμέτρηση. Ο Κούτσιας αντικαταστάθηκε στο 63ο λεπτό από τον Αμπουμπακάρ, έχοντας ήδη αφήσει το αποτύπωμά του στην αναμέτρηση. Με τα δύο τέρματα απέναντι στην Μπράγκα, έφτασε τα επτά γκολ από την αρχή της σεζόν. Η αναμέτρηση, πάντως, επεφύλασσε ακόμη περισσότερη αγωνία. Ο Όρτα χτύπησε ξανά στο 89ο λεπτό, ισοφαρίζοντας σε 2-2 κι έστειλε τις δύο ομάδες στη διαδικασία των πέναλτι, καθώς στη συγκεκριμένη φάση της διοργάνωσης δεν προβλέπεται παράταση. www.ertnews.gr

items.title: 13 ερευνητές της ευτυχίας συναντήθηκαν και συμφώνησαν σε 5 κλειδιά για να ζήσουν την «καλή ζωή»
items.titleOriginal: 13 happiness researchers met and agreed on 5 keys to living the ‘good life’
items.description: Καμία αναζήτηση στη ζωή δεν είναι μεγαλύτερη από το να ανακαλύψεις τι σε κάνει πραγματικά ευτυχισμένο. Θα ήταν κρίμα να σπαταλήσετε μια ολόκληρη ζωή γαβγίζοντας το λάθος δέντρο μόνο για να συνειδητοποιήσετε στα τελευταία σας χρόνια τι πραγματικά έχει σημασία. Αλλά δυστυχώς, δεν βρίσκουν όλοι την αληθινή ευτυχία. Μια δημοσκόπηση του 2025 της Gallup διαπίστωσε ότι μόνο το 44% των Αμερικανών είναι «πολύ ικανοποιημένοι» με τη ζωή τους, κάτω από 21 μονάδες…
items.descriptionOriginal: No quest in life is greater than finding out what truly makes you happy . It’d be a shame to waste an entire lifetime barking up the wrong tree only to realize in your final years what truly matters. But sadly, not everyone finds true happiness. A 2025 Gallup poll found that only 44% of Americans are “very satisfied” with their lives, down 21 points from 2020 and the lowest score since the poll began in 2001. To help people better understand what makes humans happy , 13 of the world’s leading well-being researchers got together earlier this year on a Zoom call. Their goal: to share what their 600 total years of happiness research and lived experience taught them about finding the good life. They documented their reflections in a research paper published in the Journal of Happiness Studies . A happy woman having coffee. Photo credit: Canva The overwhelming takeaway is that relationships are the biggest key to happiness. “Happiness emerges from a symphony of factors, but if I had to pinpoint one secret to happiness, relationships with other people might be it,” said Lara Aknin , a professor of social psychology at Simon Fraser University, who coauthored the study with Harvard University’s Säde Stenlund and Kelsey O’Connor from Luxembourg’s National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies, in a statement. “We know that having just one person you can count on is extremely consequential. Having more relationships and more communities that you feel a part of compounds that sense of well-being,” Aknin continued. The researchers’ discussion yields five key takeaways: 1. Relationships matter more than almost anything else Several researchers on the Zoom call reported consciously spending more time with loved ones after seeing the evidence from their own research. 2. More money doesn’t mean more happiness Yes, a comfortable income and financial security are important foundations—but once your basic needs are met, added income has less impact on happiness. 3. Meaningful work contributes strongly to happiness Happiness comes from doing work and activities that feel worthwhile and aligned with your values. A smiling man with his arms folded. Photo credit: Canva 4. Happiness can grow through intentional habits Several researchers said they applied findings from happiness science to their own lives, such as expressing gratitude, savoring positive experiences, investing in relationships, listening more deeply, volunteering, and being more socially engaged. 5. Happiness is not about feeling good all the time Well-being grows when people shape their lives around their values, strengths, and relationships, and learn to adapt when circumstances change. The researchers also noted that happiness isn’t just about being dealt a good hand in life. It’s about how you handle your circumstances. Leading models find that 10% of people’s happiness comes from life circumstances, such as where you grew up, relationship status, or employment. However, 40% of a person’s happiness comes from “volitional activities,” or how you choose to spend your time. Happy, smiling children. Photo credit: Canva “That leaves a lot of opportunity for people who may be more innately pessimistic to start practicing research-backed strategies like meditation or gratitude that might help them see the world in a more positive way,” Aknin said. Unfortunately, many in the U.S. are struggling to find true happiness these days. But the good news is that, according to the world’s leading minds on the subject, we can all choose to be happy, regardless of our circumstances, if we follow their research. And when one person chooses the path of happiness, others will follow. “With many large and threatening realities taking place in the world right now, I sometimes worry that the pursuit of happiness can seem trite. But one reason I remain committed to the scientific study of happiness is that happiness in and of itself predicts a number of valuable outcomes, including the motivation to help other people,” Aknin explained. The post 13 happiness researchers met and agreed on 5 keys to living the ‘good life’ appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: More than likely, you’ve had at least one teacher who helped shape the person you are today. Perhaps they exposed you to ideas that challenged you to think in a new way. Maybe they saw potential in you before you saw it in yourself. The best teachers instill skills and a joy of learning that enable students to create and grow for years to come. Nam Yun Kim was one of those teachers. She spent nearly 40 years shaping the world of classical music. Many knew Kim as the “Godmother of Korean Violin.” She was a brilliant soloist who performed all over the world. But her favorite home was in the classroom. In 2014, after almost four decades of teaching in South Korea, her students honored her with a retirement concert. Just when she thought she was giving her final bow, something unexpected happened: a bonus performance that would leave her and the audience in joyful tears. A stage filled with love and music Kim was about to leave the stage when about 100 previous and current violin students revealed themselves. They joined the full orchestra for one final, celebratory moment in honor of their mentor. Teens stood shoulder to shoulder with accomplished international professionals. The common link: they all had Kim as their teacher and had benefited from her tough lessons and kind encouragement. When the music swelled, Frank Sinatra’s iconic anthem, “My Way,” filled the concert hall. It was a tribute built from decades of collective passion, patience, and rigorous dedication. Kim’s appreciative and tearful reaction says the rest. Her life’s work was playing all around her. Why ‘My Way’ fit so well Sinatra’s song looks back on a life lived on your own terms. Kim chose to pour herself into generations of violin students in her own, unique way and accumulated decades of devoted students who blossomed from her teachings. Born in Seoul in 1949, Kim studied violin at Juilliard. In 1974, Kim won first prize at the Tibor Varga International Violin Competition. She went on to play at Carnegie Hall, the Kennedy Center, and the Sydney Opera House. Instead of continuing to tour the world as an international star, Kim returned home to South Korea in 1977 and started teaching. She gave masterclasses at Yale and the Beijing Conservatory. Over the decades, she judged top competitions, and her students rose to the top of the violin world. Some of the acclaimed performers who studied under her include Chee-Yun Kim and Yura Lee. For her artistic efforts, Kim received the Nan-Pa Music Award and the Ok-Kwan Medal from the Korean government. Tears of joy for a legendary mentor Most teachers plant seeds they may never see bloom. Kim got to witness hers flourish all at once in one unforgettable moment. The footage of the surprise serenade at her retirement concert still moves people to tears today. She spent nearly 40 years helping others develop their musical talents and got to hear the results of her students’ work during the tribute. Kim passed away in 2023 at the age of 74. The post Violin teacher of 40 years gets teary-eyed after surprise goodbye performance by her students appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: A 3rd day NASA intern found a planet with 2 suns. 7 years later, it’s still fascinating scientists.
items.description: Η ιδέα ενός πλανήτη σε τροχιά γύρω από δύο ήλιους ακούγεται σαν επιστημονική φαντασία. Πιο συγκεκριμένα, είναι μια ιδέα από το Star Wars: ο φανταστικός πλανήτης Tatooine έχει δύο ήλιους. Αλλά στην πραγματική ζωή; Οι επιστήμονες πίστευαν από καιρό ότι αυτό ήταν αδύνατο. Ωστόσο, το 2011, ανακαλύφθηκε ο πρώτος «περιφερικός» πλανήτης, όπως λέγεται. Τα επόμενα χρόνια αστρονόμος…
items.descriptionOriginal: The idea of a planet orbiting two suns sounds like science fiction. More specifically, it’s an idea from Star Wars : the fictional planet Tatooine famously has two suns. But in real life? Scientists long thought that was impossible. However, in 2011, the first “circumbinary” planet, as it’s called, was discovered. In the following years, astronomers confirmed more and more. But scientists still didn’t understand much about this rare phenomenon. In 2019, a new planet with two suns was discovered by an unexpected scientist Wolf Cukier was just a high school junior when he began a summer internship at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in 2019. Simply put, he was a data jockey. His job was to dig through extensive data on variations in star brightness captured by NASA’s TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite). On just his third day looking through the data, Cukier noticed something weird. All indications pointed to a stellar eclipse in a distant solar system called TOI 1338. A stellar eclipse is when one star passes in front of another in a binary system, or a system with two stars. “But the timing was wrong,” Cukier said, per NASA. Instead of an eclipse, he realized he was looking at a new planet. High school intern discovers planet TOI 1338 b The planet, clocked by then 17-year-old Cukier on just his third day on the job, became known as TOI 1338 b. Not the catchiest name, of course, which is why some informally call it “Wolftopia” after its discoverer. It lives about 1300 light-years away in the constellation Pictor. TOI 1338 b is a fascinating case. It orbits two stars: one noticeably larger than Earth’s Sun and the other slightly smaller. The stars orbit each other while the planet, about 6.9 times Earth’s size, orbits both. For its part, Wolftopia is extremely large but has an extremely low mass. Its density qualifies it as a “super-puff” exoplanet. Circumbinary planets like TOI 1338 b are difficult to detect. Scientists agree they are relatively common, even though we’ve confirmed only about 18 so far. But their unusual light patterns make them tricky for algorithms to identify. Luckily, the eager and very human eyes of Cukier were on the case. A paper published in The Astronomical Journal featured TOI 1338 b, and Cukier was even listed as a co-author. That makes him one of the youngest co-authors ever on a NASA-related scientific discovery. (He remains ever so slightly edged out by 16-year-old Pritvik Sinhadc , who co-authored Astrobiology Primer 3.0 in 2020.) 7 years later, Cukier and TOI 1338 b have a bright future Cukier’s story was a media hit when it first occurred about seven years ago. But the tale doesn’t end there. TOI 1338 b remains of great interest to scientists. In September 2026, the world’s most powerful telescope—the James Webb Space Telescope —set its sights on the planet to analyze its atmosphere. Though astronomers have discovered over a dozen circumbinary planets, we still don’t know much about them. The light, heat, radiation, and gravitational pull of two suns undoubtedly create weather patterns and surface conditions unlike anything scientists have seen. Once the analysis is finished and released, it can tell us more about how planets form and help us identify even more Tatooine-like circumbinary planets in the future. As for Cukier, he’s still shooting for the stars as an Astronomy and Astrophysics PhD student at the University of Chicago, no doubt motivated by the fact that a discovery on his third day on the job continues to pay dividends in the scientific community. The post A 3rd day NASA intern found a planet with 2 suns. 7 years later, it’s still fascinating scientists. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Το «I’m Not in Love» των 10cc ακούγεται σαν μια τεράστια χορωδία. Ο τρόπος που το έφτιαξαν είναι εκπληκτικός.
items.titleOriginal: 10cc’s ‘I’m Not in Love’ sounds like a huge choir. The way they made it is astonishing.
items.description: Υπάρχει μια εμβληματική στιγμή κοντά στην αρχή του "I'm Not in Love" του βρετανικού ποπ γκρουπ 10cc, όταν το τραγούδι φαίνεται να επιπλέει σε άλλη διάσταση. Η φωνή του Eric Stewart περιβάλλεται από ένα υπνωτιστικό, ονειρικό πλύσιμο των φωνητικών "ahh", κάνοντας την αίσθηση ότι μια ολόκληρη χορωδία κατέβηκε από τους ουρανούς για να κάνει ντουέτο μαζί του. Εκτός… δεν υπήρχε χορωδία. Το αποτέλεσμα προήλθε από…
items.descriptionOriginal: There’s an iconic moment near the beginning of British pop group 10cc’s “I’m Not in Love” when the song seems to float into another dimension. Eric Stewart’s voice is surrounded by a hypnotic, dreamy wash of “ahh” vocals, making it feel like an entire choir came down from the heavens to duet with him. Except…there was no choir. The effect came from the band members’ voices, a 16-track machine, a pile of tape loops, and a mixing console that essentially turned it all into a singular musical instrument. The more you learn about how this song was made, the more impressive it becomes. As it is with so many great songs, “I’m Not in Love” nearly ended up in the trash “I’m Not in Love” didn’t initially have that ethereal-sounding piece. Stewart, along with 10cc co-singer and bassist Gary Gouldman, originally wrote it as a more rhythmic, bossa nova-style piece. Kevin Godley and Lol Creme, the other half of 10cc, famously thought the song was “ crap ,” so the project was abandoned altogether. That is, until Kathy Redfern, secretary of Strawberry Studios, stepped in. Stewart recalled he kept hearing multiple people around their recording studio singing the melody, which made him think the tune had promise after all. Then Redfern came up to him directly and said, “Why didn’t you finish that song? I really love it. It’s the nicest thing you’ve ever done.” He knew then the group needed to take a second look. Godley and Creme agreed, on the condition that they try again using only their voices. That experiment would change everything. A choir built one note at a time The band members gathered around a microphone and sang individual notes together. They recorded each note repeatedly, layering their voices. Godley later estimated that the finished effect held around 250 of these loops. The recordings were then mixed down into “super notes” and cut into tape loops (we, of course, do this all digitally today, but in the ’70s, they did it by hand). Stewart told Sound on Sound that they created 12 loops, each containing a sustained vocal note. Those loops were then fed back into the multitrack recording and routed to individual faders on the mixing console. The notes were arranged so the band could create chords by raising and lowering different faders. Stewart, Godley, Gouldman, and Creme were, essentially, playing the mixing desk and an enormous keyboard. Godley later compared what they had created to “an enormous high-end Mellotron ,” except that instead of pressing keys, the band would move faders to bring vocal notes in and out. Because the individual vocal loops were completely isolated, traces of them remained beneath the main chords. Rather than remove them, 10cc kept them in, giving the final recording a hazy, electronic quality despite being made up entirely of human voices. This sound somehow perfectly filled the spaces where the instruments weren’t playing. Or, as Godley described it, filled the song’s “air.” After the recording was fully done, Stewart looked around at his bandmates and said, “What have we created? This is brilliant.” They agreed that they had stumbled onto something magical. They only needed one more thing to fully bring it to life It’s also worth noting that Redfern not only saved the song from being left unfinished; she also sang on it. During the dramatic break near the end, the music drops away, and a woman whispers, “Big boys don’t cry.” The woman is Redfern. Creme came up with this idea, thinking the song would benefit from a woman’s voice. Redfern wasn’t particularly eager to perform, but the band convinced her that her “gorgeous” speaking voice was the last important piece of the puzzle. After only a couple of takes, she nailed it, and “clinched” the track. She rightfully received a gold record for her contribution to a song that stayed on the U.K. Singles Chart for two weeks and peaked at number two on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100. The song’s cinematic sound gave it not only a long radio life, but a long life onscreen, too. “I’m Not in Love” has appeared in movies including The Virgin Suicides , Deuce Bigalow: Male Gigolo , Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason , He’s Just Not That Into You, and Stuber . It also appears in Guardians of the Galaxy , where a young Peter Quill listens to it through his headphones while floating in space. Nowadays, we can probably create this kind of sound with a few taps in some highfalutin app. But the original’s experimental, hands-on approach is what makes it so one-of-a-kind. It goes to show that the best songs often don’t just tell a great story; they have a great story behind them, too. The post 10cc’s ‘I’m Not in Love’ sounds like a huge choir. The way they made it is astonishing. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: Giant heat pump turns paper mill waste heat into 248°F steam with less fossil fuel
items.description: Οι μηχανικοί μόλις παρουσίασαν μια ισχυρή αντλία θερμότητας 1,2 μεγαβάτ (MW) που μπορεί να μετατρέψει την απορριπτόμενη θερμότητα από την παραγωγή χαρτιού σε βιομηχανικό ατμό σε θερμοκρασίες περίπου 248 βαθμών Φαρενάιτ (120 βαθμούς Κελσίου). Η αντλία θερμότητας κατασκευάστηκε από μια ερευνητική ομάδα με τη συμμετοχή του Fraunhofer Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies (IEG) στο Ger…
items.descriptionOriginal: Engineers have just unveiled a powerful 1.2-megawatt (MW) heat pump that can convert waste heat from paper production into industrial steam at temperatures of around 248 degrees Fahrenheit (120 degrees Celsius). The heat pump was made by a research team involving the Fraunhofer Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies (IEG) in Germany. It was tested at a paper mill run by Felix Schoeller GmbH & Co. KG in Weißenborn, Hesse. The trial was conducted under the EU-funded PUSH2HEAT project. The system uses otherwise wasted heat to produce steam for industrial processes. According to the institute, it could reduce carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions by up to 600 tons annually. This means it could also lower natural gas reliance. “Industrial companies need solutions that combine climate protection, energy supply security, and competitiveness,” Reuven Paitazoglou, the project’s manager, said. “High-temperature heat pumps make it possible to economically harness previously unused energy sources for production.” From waste heat to steam Industrial processes operate steam systems well above atmospheric pressure at temperatures exceeding 212 degrees Fahrenheit (100 degrees Celsius). In most cases, producing this steam involves burning fossil fuels, especially natural gas. On the other hand, fossil fuel combustion releases CO2 and other greenhouse gases that drive climate change and air pollution. To address this challenge, the team developed a two-stage heat pump capable of upgrading low-temperature waste heat into usable industrial steam. The system captures excess heat from paper production at temperatures ranging from 86 to 158 degrees Fahrenheit (30 to 70 degrees Celsius). It then raises the temperature to approximately 248 degrees Fahrenheit. During its first approximately 300 operating hours in 2026, the pump achieved an average steam output of around 700 kilowatts (kW). It also produced roughly 1.2 tons of steam per hour at a pressure of around 2.3 bar. The researchers reported a performance factor of 2.30. In simple terms the system delivered more than twice as much useful heat as the electrical energy required to operate it. The installation could prevent up to 600 tons of CO2 emissions a year if operated for 4,000 to 5,000 hours. That could cut CO2 emissions by around 220 lbs (100 kilograms) per megawatt-hour (MWh) of heat compared to natural gas steam production. Wider industrial potential The demo was part of the EU-funded PUSH2HEAT project , which explores ways to reuse industrial waste heat. Although it primarily focuses on paper and chemical production, the technology could also find applications in the pharmaceutical and food industries. Fraunhofer IEG coordinated the scientific aspects of the tests and came up with a monitoring system to assess its performance. The team examined how the pump could be integrated into existing production processes and steam networks. Paitazoglou emphasized the importance of expanding the technology’s use. “The demonstration plant in Weißenborn lays important groundwork for the future use of this technology in other industrial applications,” he disclosed in a press release . Full-load tests began in September 2026. The team plans to evaluate the system under real industrial conditions for one year. Further improvements are expected before the project ends in 2027.

items.descriptionOriginal: A luxury car manufacturer is advancing a new cell chemistry for EVs. Mercedes-Benz is taking steps to combine lithium manganese oxide (LMO) and nickel manganese cobalt oxide (NMC). This cathode-material combination uses a higher proportion of manganese and less cobalt and nickel, enabling an attractive balance between energy density and cost. At the same time, this chemical combination forms the technological bridge to the manganese-rich cathode materials of the future. With lithium nickel manganese oxide (LNMO), Mercedes-Benz is advancing another promising cell chemistry. It would eliminate the need for cobalt, require significantly less nickel than today’s NMC cells and offer the potential to combine high energy density with attractive costs. High-voltage capability of LNMO-based cell chemistry The key would be the high-voltage capability of LNMO-based cell chemistry , which could operate at voltages of up to five volts. Compared with LFP, range advantages of up to 30 percent may be possible at comparable weight and packaging space, according to a press release. Mercedes‑Benz aims to develop even more compact and lighter battery systems while maintaining the same or even higher performance. These systems open up new possibilities for vehicle design and interior layout. Furthermore, manganese-based cell technologies can reduce reliance on critical raw materials. Developing in-house cell chemistry platforms increases flexibility in responding to technological developments, market changes and regulatory requirements, as per the release. “No technology shapes the character of a vehicle as much as the powertrain, whether fully electric or hybrid,” said Jörg Bartels, Vice President, Powertrain Development, Mercedes‑Benz AG. “Our customers around the world have different needs and expectations. That is why we are committed to utilising the best technology in such a way that it delivers tangible added value and inspires our customers. True innovation arises where technical excellence translates into an intuitive driving experience and creates an almost instinctive emotional connection between the driver and the vehicle.” The company is driving forward the development of solid-state batteries in collaboration with its strategic partners, Factorial Energy and ProLogium. With Factorial Energy, a lithium-metal solid-state battery has already been developed and tested for the first time under real-world driving conditions in an EQS. The development vehicle covered 1,205 kilometres from Stuttgart to Malmö without recharging, thereby demonstrating the technology’s potential for long ranges. Next generation of solid-state cells Mercedes‑Benz revealed that it’s investigating the next generation of solid-state cells with several partners, including ProLogium’s next-generation cells. The focus is on extensive testing of Gen4 cell technology in terms of performance, safety and thermal properties. The aim is to assess their potential for future series production. In addition, tests are being carried out with solid-state cells from other partners and those developed in-house, incorporating motorsports know-how from the Formula 1 powertrain experts in the UK.

items.descriptionOriginal: Being in a healthy, loving relationship usually involves two people who can share emotional reciprocity. There is patience, understanding, and peace. But some people often feel like they are “too much” in relationships. This can come with feelings of anxiety and disrupt trust and growth—whether the relationship is with a romantic partner, family member, or friend. During a recent appearance on the Zach Sang Show , motivational expert Mel Robbins broke down exactly why some people feel they are “too much.” Robbins explained it with an analogy called the “10-gallon people” theory that Oprah Winfrey first shared with her. View this post on Instagram The ‘10-gallon people’ theory In the clip, Robbins explained that understanding the “10-gallon people” theory has been “so transformational for me.” Robbins added that she learned it from Oprah, who first heard about it from Bishop T.D. Jakes. Jakes helped Oprah apply it to her complicated relationship with her mom. The theory uses measurement sizes to describe people: There are “10-gallon people” and “pint people.” “‘Ten-gallon people’ need 10 gallons of love, and 10 gallons of attention, and 10 gallons of excitement, and 10 gallons of energy—and 10 gallons is what I need,” Robbins said. “If you’re a ‘10-gallon person’ looking for 10 gallons of love, and you’re dealing with a person that has a pint-size capacity because of their past or maybe because of what they’re dealing with in the present, you’re not going to feel satisfied,” she added. Robbins went on to say that she is definitely a “10-gallon person,” and there are “lots of people in my life that are ‘pint-size.’ And they’ll pour the entire pint that they have to give into me. But I’m not satisfied.” She called it “sad,” because that person with the pint-size capacity gave “everything they had to give. And there’s nothing wrong with somebody who’s pint-sized,” she explained. View this post on Instagram Avoiding resentments regarding capacity Unfortunately, this can lead to resentment. Robbins explains that this can leave the 10-gallon person feeling like the pint-size person “didn’t give me enough.” However, it was all they had to give—their everything. “And you didn’t see it because you were looking for something different,” said Robbins. She added that she has learned “it’s not better or worse to be pint-size or 10-gallon—it just is.” Robbins said it comes down to having an awareness about which one you are, based on both past and present circumstances. For example, 10-gallon people may become pint-sized when things happen in life, such as a friend dealing with a cancer diagnosis or another struggle. Rather than being judgmental and taking a step back, Robbins explained with her own “Let Them” theory that it’s important to “let them show up differently, and let me ask myself: How do I want to show up? What kind of friend do I want to be? Do I want to write this person off, or do I want to pick up the phone and ask, ‘You don’t seem like yourself. Everything going okay?’ And then you can decide what to do next.” Oprah explains the ‘10-gallon people’ theory During a September 2026 appearance on The Mel Robbins Podcast, Oprah introduced the concept to Robbins and explained more about how she related to the 10-gallon people theory in regard to her relationship with her mother. “I’m a 10-gallon person, and you’re a 10-gallon person, and a lot of you are 10-gallon people trying to get 10 gallons worth of love from pint-sized people who cannot carry the 10 gallons,” Oprah said. “They can’t even carry the gallon.” She added that when expecting to gain 10-gallon “love, responses, reception, acceptance” from people who have a “pint-sized ability,” they “don’t have it.” Oprah added it’s about recognizing that, and changing the focus to what they have by asking yourself: “Can I accept you exactly as you are, with what you do have?” “With my mother, she could cook, she made some incredible collard greens, and could make cornbread like nobody else—and that was the way she offered love,” she said, explaining that people in her generation or others may be familiar with this. “Because I provided for you, that was love. You had food on the table, you had shelter, you weren’t on the streets. That was all I had,” Oprah explained, connecting that both her mom and grandmother were maids and domestic workers who were “giving all your energy to taking care of other people’s kids, putting on the face for them, wearing the mask for them. And by the time you came home, you had nothing left for me. I recognize that now, and I forgive that.” The post Motivational expert shares the ‘10-gallon people’ theory to explain why some feel ‘too much’ in relationships appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Όταν η Stevie Nicks κάθισε στην καρέκλα του μακιγιάζ για τη φωτογράφισή της στο Rolling Stone με την πανέξυπνη Annie Leibovitz, κανείς δεν μπορούσε να ξέρει ότι θα ακολουθούσε τέτοια μαγεία. Σίγουρα, οι ίδιες οι φωτογραφίες ήταν αιθέριες, με τον Nicks με ένα ρέον λευκό φόρεμα, σαθρές μπότες και συντροφιά με το cockatoo, φυσικά. Ήταν, όμως, το αυθόρμητο τραγούδι της μαζί με έναν αυτοσχέδιο ντε…
items.descriptionOriginal: When Stevie Nicks sat down in the makeup chair for her Rolling Stone shoot with the brilliant Annie Leibovitz , no one could have known such magic would follow. Sure, the photos themselves were ethereal, with Nicks in a flowing white dress, slouchy boots, and cockatoo companion, of course. But it was her guttural singing along with an impromptu demo before the shoot that has especially stood the test of time. Luckily, the cameras caught this all on video, and the clip continues to delight fans. The year was 1981, and Nicks was doing promotional photos for her first solo album, Bella Donna . She plopped down for a dash of rosy powder, and as her eyelids were getting lined, she started to sing, as though she couldn’t keep it caged. For one, it wasn’t her style. If Nicks had something on her mind, it often came out as an echoing, heart-wrenching war cry. It never mattered if she was on stage or behind it. ‘Don’t blame it on me’ The makeup artist seemed to realize in real time that she was witnessing the genesis stage of a brilliant piece of art. The music kicks in, and she locked eyes with Nicks, even doing a little dance, as if to say, “I hear you; keep going.” “Don’t blame it on me,” Nicks sang, with a tiny smile as she continued her eye contact. “Blame it on my wild heart.” In a piece for The New Yorker , Amanda Petrusich wrote, “Nicks, in which she sits on a stool having her makeup done, wearing a white dress with spaghetti straps. She begins to sing. Soon, someone is messing with a piano; one of her backup singers joins in with a harmony. The makeup artist gamely tries to continue with her work, before giving up. While the studio recording of ‘Wild Heart’ is saturated, almost wet, this version is all air, all joy.” View this post on Instagram Petrusich shared her perception that Nicks simply couldn’t help herself. “What affects me most about the video is how profoundly Nicks appears to love singing. Her voice has an undulating, galloping quality. It is as if, once it’s started up, there’s no slowing down, no stopping; the car is careering down a mountain, with no brakes. You can see on her face how good it feels just to let go.” Evolution of a song A shorter version of the same clip was posted on Threads by filmmaker Ryan Booth, who shared how much it means to him and anyone else who has ever been behind the camera or in front of greatness. “Every time I stumble on this video of Stevie Nicks backstage at a Rolling Stone photoshoot as she ad-libs a yet-to-be-written ‘Wild Heart,’ I download it. I have dozens of copies at this point.” Booth explained in the comments that Nicks’ Fleetwood Mac bandmate (and complicated ex) Lindsey Buckingham recorded the demo. “It’s a demo of a track Lindsey had laid down earlier that day. In another version, you can more clearly hear her say ‘we were singing to this in the car on the way over.’” The track wasn’t just any track, and the people singing harmony weren’t just any backup singers. The music was from an early demo of Buckingham’s “Can’t Go Back,” which at the time had the title “Suma’s Walk.” (It was all an evolutionary soup for the song “Wild Heart,” which would appear on Nicks’ second solo album.) Magic harmony Booth shared, “The woman singing harmony is the dark-haired woman who you can see when the cam pulls out wide. Lori Perry.” He reiterated what Nicks reportedly said. “You can hear Stevie say that ‘we were singing this line in the car on the way over,’ and ‘this is the chorus – we’ll figure the rest out tomorrow.’” Many in the comments expressed that this raw version was better than what appeared on the studio album. “This version of Wild Heart is so much better than the one that was released. IMO. These vocals are the magic of this song and they got lost in the final recording.” In comments on the YouTube clip, a few pointed out how beautiful Nicks sounded and what a special moment it must have been for everyone in the room. “There will NEVER be a rock singer that can outdo Stevie’s alto vibrato and harmonization. You can’t learn that. She was born to give us this gift. Ps…if she was singing looking me right in the face like that, I’d be a blubbering mess.” The post In 1981, Stevie Nicks sang an unfinished ‘Wild Heart’ in a makeup chair. It’s pure, raw magic. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Renewable Natural Gas Is Turning Everyday Waste Into Cleaner Fuel for Businesses Reading Time: 3 minutes Renewable Natural Gas Is Turning Everyday Waste Into Cleaner Fuel for Businesses The shift towards sustainability has led to numerous innovations in the way that companies operate. One of the most exciting developments is the use of renewable natural gas (RNG). RNG is created by capturing methane from sources such as agricultural runoff, landfills, and wastewater treatment plants. This not only reduces the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere but also creates a new source of energy for those facilities. Adding RNG to your natural gas procurement for businesses is a straightforward way to hit green targets without risking downtime. It tackles organic waste head-on and acts as an easy, drop-in replacement for fossil fuels. How Everyday Waste Transforms into Power The journey from refuse to resource is a fascinating one that involves the capture and processing of methane gas from decomposing organic matter before it escapes into the atmosphere. Instead of allowing this potent greenhouse gas to contribute to climate change, facilities that use anaerobic digesters are able to break down dairy manure, food scraps, and wastewater sludge. The biogas that is produced from these facilities undergoes a purification process to remove moisture, carbon dioxide, and other elements from the gas. The resulting gas is structurally identical to natural gas, allowing it to be injected into existing gas infrastructure and utilized by commercial fleets and manufacturing plants without any need for modification to their equipment. Evaluating the Financial and Environmental Dual Benefits Shifting to this circular energy model offers companies a unique opportunity to tackle two major corporate objectives simultaneously: minimizing ecological impact and stabilizing operational costs. Because RNG is domestically produced from continuous waste streams, it can help shield commercial consumers from the extreme price volatility often associated with global fossil fuel markets. When executives sit down to analyze their overall natural gas procurement strategies, incorporating a renewable component proves highly advantageous for long-term budget forecasting. Furthermore, utilizing this upgraded biogas significantly lowers a company’s direct carbon footprint, allowing brands to authentically market their sustainability achievements to an increasingly eco-conscious consumer base. Overcoming Adoption Barriers and Infrastructure Myths One of the most common misconceptions about the implementation of alternative fuels is that companies will have to invest millions of dollars into new machinery and infrastructure. However, since the upgraded biomethane is chemically identical to the geological methane that now fuels the majority of the nation’s cities and industries, the fuel can be easily implemented into the existing pipeline system without any need for the implementation of new machinery or infrastructure. Also, since the fuel is chemically identical to the existing fuel, the implementation of this new fuel source will not require the implementation of new infrastructure. Instead, the companies can simply update their purchasing agreements with the companies that produce the fuel to implement the new fuel source into their operations. Strategic Sourcing for Corporate Sustainability Goals A sophisticated strategy is needed to source sustainable energy, especially given the growing demand for environmentally friendly substitutes in a number of heavy industries. To make sure they are obtaining genuine environmental attributes in addition to their physical fuel supply, corporate buyers must negotiate a complicated web of producers, marketers, and local utility regulations. When handling natural gas procurement for businesses, look for suppliers who can trace their biomethane straight from the farm or landfill to your facility. Securing these transparent contracts makes it much easier to prove emission cuts to stakeholders and meet strict climate regulations. Embracing the Circular Economy of Tomorrow Another way in which the use of upgraded biogas can benefit commercial enterprises is in reducing their reliance on traditional fossil fuels. The use of biogas as a fuel source for these companies can help to significantly reduce their carbon footprint without any changes to their daily operations. As the technology to capture and refine methane improves, the availability and affordability of biogas will continue to increase. Companies that incorporate biogas into their energy portfolios will be at an advantage compared to their competitors who do not take such steps towards sustainability. The post Renewable Natural Gas Is Turning Everyday Waste Into Cleaner Fuel for Businesses appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: In science, the fastest path to the future sometimes requires digging through the past. Researchers at Sweden’s Linköping University used artificial intelligence to search decades of scientific archives and uncovered 33 previously overlooked MXene forms. These ultra-thin, high-performance materials were first officially recognized in 2011, making the recovery of these hidden compositions a major step forward for materials science. The team created a greener synthesis method that produces MXenes in seconds at room temperature, using less water and fewer hazardous chemicals. This advance improves scalability for widespread commercial applications. Finding the new forms The findings reveal that certain materials capable of transforming clean tech may have been sitting on dusty digital shelves since the 1970s. “We need to look both backward and forwards to accelerate materials science. There’s so much information in the literature that we’re not aware of. We as researchers sometimes reinvent the wheel and claim to have made great discoveries – but then it turns out they were already made in Germany, for example, in the 1970s,” said Johanna Rosén, Professor of Materials Physics at Linköping University, LiU. Early researchers synthesized the precursor parent crystals as far back as the 1970s, but the materials remained hidden in archives because the scientific framework for two-dimensional physics did not yet exist. At the time, scientists lacked both the conceptual framework for single-atom exfoliation and advanced characterization tools like high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopes. Therefore. experts earlier documented these complex crystal structures without realizing their ultra-thin 2D potential. MXenes are two-dimensional materials consisting of atom-thin layers of metals combined with carbon or nitrogen. MXenes have a massive surface area relative to their weight, as a single millimeter of the material can pack millions of stacked sheets. Greener, scalable manufacturing This unique architecture drives powerful chemical reactions, making them prime candidates for battery energy storage, water purification, telecommunications, and biomedical devices. Researchers unlocked two major breakthroughs alongside expanding the material family tree. They developed a greener synthesis process that creates MXenes in seconds without external heat, reducing toxic chemicals and water use. The team also introduced magnetic properties to MXenes through the addition of rare earth elements. It opens new possibilities for advanced data storage and electronics. As scalable, low-impact manufacturing methods take hold, these rediscovered materials could soon transition from lab-bench curiosities to commercial workhorses for global sustainability. “MXenes can have a wide range of useful properties, many with potential applications in sustainability. Discovering new compositions gives us the opportunity to explore even more possibilities for how these materials can be used,” said Ali Saffar Shamshirgar, researcher at LiU and first author. However, turning advanced materials from lab success into commercial products often falters at the production stage, where slow manufacturing and harsh chemical inputs make mass production prohibitively expensive and unsafe. The development of a rapid room-temperature synthesis method could remove this primary hurdle for MXenes . Manufacturers can scale output efficiently as energy-intensive heating is eliminated and chemical waste is reduced. This shift could help transform a niche experimental material into a viable, cost-effective component for commercial energy and electronic devices. The results were published in the journal Science.

items.descriptionOriginal: Μια σπάνια πρώτη έκδοση του βιβλίου «Το λιοντάρι, η μάγισσα και η ντουλάπα» από «Τα Χρονικά της Νάρνια» του C.S. Lewis πωλήθηκε έναντι 1.000 λιρών, αφού εντοπίστηκε εντελώς τυχαία σε φιλανθρωπικό κατάστημα στη Βρετανία. Το αντίτυπο, που εκδόθηκε το 1950 και αποτελεί το πρώτο βιβλίο της διάσημης σειράς «Τα Χρονικά της Νάρνια», βρέθηκε στο κατάστημα βιβλίων της οργάνωσης Oxfam στην πόλη Τρούρο, στην Κορνουάλη. Η ανακάλυψη έγινε από την εθελόντρια Τζέιν Ρίκαρντ, η οποία ξεχώρισε τον παλιό τόμο ανάμεσα σε βιβλία που είχαν μόλις δωριστεί. Το βιβλίο αναρτήθηκε στη διαδικτυακή πλατφόρμα πωλήσεων της φιλανθρωπικής οργάνωσης και δεν άργησε να βρει αγοραστή. Για το κατάστημα, η πώληση αποτέλεσε μια ιδιαίτερα σημαντική επιτυχία, καθώς τα έσοδα θα διατεθούν για την υποστήριξη ανθρώπων που έχουν ανάγκη. Η τυχαία ανακάλυψη που οδήγησε σε πώληση 1.000 λιρών Η εθελόντρια της Oxfam, Τζέιν Ρίκαρντ, λέει ότι έμεινε άναυδη όταν εντόπισε στο ράφι την πρώτη έκδοση του βιβλίου, που κυκλοφόρησε το 1950. Η Τζέιν Ρίκαρντ ξεφύλλιζε βιβλία που είχαν προσφερθεί ως δωρεές, όταν παρατήρησε τον συγκεκριμένο τόμο. Αρχικά, δεν γνώριζε ότι επρόκειτο για κάτι ιδιαίτερο, ωστόσο αποφάσισε να εξετάσει προσεκτικότερα την έκδοσή του. «Έμοιαζε με παλιό αντίτυπο. Κοίταξα στο εσωτερικό για να δω αν ήταν επανέκδοση, αλλά δεν ήταν, και ενθουσιάστηκα», ανέφερε, περιγράφοντας πώς ξεκίνησε η αναζήτησή της. Στη συνέχεια, αναζήτησε στο διαδίκτυο πληροφορίες για τα χαρακτηριστικά μιας πρώτης έκδοσης και διαπίστωσε ότι το βιβλίο που κρατούσε στα χέρια της ταίριαζε στην περιγραφή. Όπως είπε, όταν συνειδητοποίησε τι είχε βρει, «της έπεσε το σαγόνι». Η ίδια εξήγησε ότι μια τόσο μεγάλη αξία είναι κάτι πρωτόγνωρο για το κατάστημα. «Λαμβάνουμε εξαιρετικές δωρεές και δεν είναι ασυνήθιστο να έχουμε ένα βιβλίο αξίας 30 ή 50 λιρών. Όμως, οι 1.000 λίρες είναι κάτι που δεν έχει ξανασυμβεί», σημείωσε. Μάλιστα, η εθελόντρια θεωρεί ότι η ανακάλυψη είχε και μια δόση τύχης, καθώς συνήθως εργάζεται πίσω από τον πάγκο ή στον χώρο του καταστήματος και δεν είχε κάποιον ιδιαίτερο λόγο να αναζητήσει βιβλία στο συγκεκριμένο ράφι. Διαβάστε ακόμα Η συνεργασία των εθελοντών για την πώληση Ο υπεύθυνος του καταστήματος Oxfam Books στο Τρούρο, Μπάρναμπι Άτγουελ, δήλωσε έκπληκτος όταν είδε την Τζέιν να ξεχωρίζει τον τόμο ανάμεσα σε πολλά βιβλία που έμοιαζαν μεταξύ τους. Όπως εξήγησε, ένας ακόμη εθελοντής έλεγξε την αξία του βιβλίου και διαπίστωσε ότι μια πρώτη έκδοση μπορούσε να ξεπεράσει τις 1.000 λίρες ακόμη και χωρίς το προστατευτικό εξώφυλλο. Ακολούθησαν επιπλέον έλεγχοι από άλλα μέλη της ομάδας, τα οποία συμφώνησαν με την εκτίμηση. Στη συνέχεια, ένας εθελοντής συνέταξε την περιγραφή του βιβλίου, ενώ ο Άτγουελ φωτογράφισε τον τόμο και τον ανάρτησε προς πώληση στην τιμή των 1.000 λιρών. «Ήταν πραγματικά μια ομαδική προσπάθεια», ανέφερε, προσθέτοντας ότι όλοι χάρηκαν ιδιαίτερα όταν ολοκληρώθηκε η πώληση. Σε ένδειξη ευγνωμοσύνης, ο υπεύθυνος ευχαρίστησε επανειλημμένα την Τζέιν και της προσέφερε ένα μπουκέτο λουλούδια σε πρόσφατη συνάντηση του προσωπικού και των εθελοντών του καταστήματος. «Είναι υπέροχο να γνωρίζουμε ότι αυτά τα χρήματα θα χρησιμοποιηθούν για να βοηθήσουν ανθρώπους που έχουν ανάγκη», δήλωσε. Η ιστορία πίσω από τα «Χρονικά της Νάρνια» Το «Το λιοντάρι, η μάγισσα και η ντουλάπα» κυκλοφόρησε το 1950 και αποτελεί το πρώτο βιβλίο της σειράς «Τα Χρονικά της Νάρνια», την οποία έγραψε ο Βρετανός συγγραφέας C.S. Lewis. Η σειρά αποτελείται από επτά μυθιστορήματα, που εκδόθηκαν από το 1950 έως το 1956. Οι ιστορίες φαντασίας απέκτησαν παγκόσμια δημοτικότητα και μεταφέρθηκαν πολλές φορές στον κινηματογράφο και στο θέατρο. Το ενδιαφέρον για τον μαγικό κόσμο της Νάρνια συνεχίζεται μέχρι σήμερα, με νέες οπτικοακουστικές διασκευές, μεταξύ των οποίων και παραγωγή του Netflix. Η πρόσφατη ανακάλυψη στην Κορνουάλη δείχνει ότι ακόμη και ένα βιβλίο που βρίσκεται ανάμεσα σε συνηθισμένες δωρεές μπορεί να αποδειχθεί πολύτιμο συλλεκτικό αντικείμενο, προσφέροντας παράλληλα σημαντική οικονομική ενίσχυση σε έναν φιλανθρωπικό σκοπό. items.titleOriginal: Invisible light cracks 60-year-old quantum puzzle in superconductor whirlpools
items.description: Χρησιμοποιώντας μια δέσμη αόρατου φωτός, οι ερευνητές έχουν αποκωδικοποιήσει τις μαγνητικές δίνες που σχηματίζονται μέσα στους υπεραγωγούς. Μπορεί να βοηθήσει τους μηχανικούς να κατασκευάσουν πιο ανθεκτικά εξαρτήματα για δίκτυα ισχύος, σαρωτές MRI και επιταχυντές σωματιδίων. «Για να βελτιώσουν τους υπεραγωγούς, οι επιστήμονες πρέπει να καταλάβουν τι περιέχουν οι δίνες και πώς συμπεριφέρονται», δήλωσε ο Girsh Blumberg.…
items.descriptionOriginal: Using a beam of invisible light, researchers have decoded the magnetic whirlpools that form within superconductors. It can help engineers build more resilient components for power grids, MRI scanners, and particle accelerators. “To improve superconductors, scientists need to understand what vortices contain and how they behave,” said Girsh Blumberg, a distinguished professor of physics and astronomy at Rutgers and co-author of the study, published in Physical Review Letters. Superconductors are celebrated for carrying electric currents with zero resistance. Yet exposure to strong magnetic fields creates microscopic disruptions known as vortices. Inside each vortex, electrical currents swirl around a weakened core where superconductivity breaks down. “It’s like Swiss cheese, with many holes,” added Blumberg. Proving a difficult theory When these vortices shift, the material leaks electrical energy as heat. Physicists have long wanted to peer inside these cores to see how trapped particles behave. Theorists had already predicted that particles inside each vortex would settle into stepped quantum energy levels, much like the rungs of a ladder. However, proving this experimentally has been notoriously difficult because the energy rungs in most materials blur together. To solve the puzzle, the Rutgers team manufactured an iron-based compound containing tellurium and selenium. Using layer-by-layer atomic deposition, professors Seongshik Oh, Hee Taek Yi, and their colleagues created flawless crystalline films just 40 nanometers thick—roughly a thousand times thinner than a human hair. The narrow cores of this compound kept the quantum rungs spaced cleanly apart. The experiments then moved to Tallinn, Estonia, where the films were chilled to minus 438 degrees Fahrenheit under intense magnetic fields. Scientists fired terahertz radiation, a form of low-frequency invisible light, straight through the ultra-thin samples. Testing the two variations The team manipulated the polarization of the light beam. Light waves can twist clockwise or counterclockwise as they travel. The researchers discovered that the trapped particles divided cleanly into two distinct groups. One group reacted only to the left-handed spiral, while the other reacted only to the right-handed twist. “That difference allowed the researchers to tell the two groups apart and study each one separately,” noted a press release . “Using their light measurements and mathematical calculations, the researchers estimated the size of the vortices and how long the particles’ responses to light lasted.” “They also estimated how strongly the vortices resist changes in speed or direction and how strong a magnetic field would disrupt superconductivity for each group of particles.” The team also tested two variations of their chemical recipe with different amounts of selenium. Although both samples began superconducting at nearly identical temperatures, their internal mechanics were strikingly different. One recipe produced four times as many particles of the first group as the second, while the other recipe yielded an even split. The results show that superconductors with the same operating temperatures can conceal vastly different internal dynamics. By isolating these trapped particles with polarized light, researchers now have a precise method to fine-tune materials for future heavy-duty electrical technologies.

items.descriptionOriginal: Οι ραγδαίες εξελίξεις στην αντιμετώπιση του σακχαρώδη διαβήτη , της παχυσαρκίας και των καρδιαγγειακών νοσημάτω ν, αλλά και η στενή σχέση τους με τη χρόνια νεφρική νόσο, βρίσκονται στο επίκεντρο του 5ου Συνεδρίου « Προσεγγίζοντας τον Σακχαρώδη Διαβήτη στον Καρδιοπαθή », που πραγματοποιείται στις 30 και 31 Οκτωβρίου 2026, στο Κεντρικό Κτίριο του Εθνικού και Καποδιστριακού Πανεπιστημίου Αθηνών (Προπύλαια). Το συνέδριο συνδιοργανώνεται από τη Γ’ Πανεπιστημιακή Καρδιολογική Κλινική του ΕΚΠΑ και τη Συμμαχία για την Καταπολέμηση της Παχυσαρκίας (Action4obesity), σε μια περίοδο κατά την οποία η καρδιομεταβολική ιατρική αλλάζει με γρήγορους ρυθμούς. Νέες φαρμακευτικές θεραπείες, σύγχρονα διαγνωστικά εργαλεία και καινοτόμες τεχνολογίες δημιουργούν νέες δυνατότητες για την πρόληψη και αντιμετώπιση νοσημάτων που συχνά συνυπάρχουν και αλληλοεπηρεάζονται. Η αξιοποίησή τους, ωστόσο, προϋποθέτει στενότερη συνεργασία μεταξύ διαφορετικών ιατρικών ειδικοτήτων και μια περισσότερο εξατομικευμένη προσέγγιση του ασθενούς. Από τον διαβήτη στην καρδιά και τους νεφρούς Στόχος του συνεδρίου είναι να αναδείξει τις νεότερες εξελίξεις στην καρδιομεταβολική ιατρική, ενισχύοντας τον διάλογο μεταξύ των επαγγελματιών υγείας που εμπλέκονται στην πρόληψη, τη διάγνωση και τη θεραπεία του σακχαρώδη διαβήτη, της παχυσαρκίας, των καρδιαγγειακών νοσημάτων και της χρόνιας νεφρικής νόσου. Το επιστημονικό πρόγραμμα περιλαμβάνει διαλέξεις, συζητήσεις με ειδικούς, παρουσιάσεις κλινικών περιστατικών και ανάλυση των νεότερων επιστημονικών δεδομένων. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση θα δοθεί στην πρόληψη και την έγκαιρη διάγνωση, στις σύγχρονες φαρμακευτικές επιλογές, στην εξατομικευμένη διαχείριση των ασθενών, καθώς και στις δυνατότητες που προσφέρουν οι νέες τεχνολογίες στην καθημερινή κλινική πράξη. Βήμα και για τη νέα έρευνα Για πρώτη φορά στο πλαίσιο του συνεδρίου εγκαινιάζεται και η υποβολή πρωτότυπων ερευνητικών εργασιών, οι οποίες θα μπορούν να παρουσιαστούν μετά από αξιολόγηση. Επαγγελματίες υγείας, ερευνητές και νέοι επιστήμονες καλούνται να παρουσιάσουν ερευνητικά και κλινικά δεδομένα γύρω από τον σακχαρώδη διαβήτη, την παχυσαρκία, τα καρδιαγγειακά νοσήματα και τη χρόνια νεφρική νόσο, δημιουργώντας ένα επιπλέον πεδίο ανταλλαγής επιστημονικής γνώσης και εμπειρίας. Το 5ο Συνέδριο «Προσεγγίζοντας τον Σακχαρώδη Διαβήτη στον Καρδιοπαθή» φιλοδοξεί έτσι να αναδείξει τη σύγχρονη αντίληψη ότι η αντιμετώπιση των καρδιομεταβολικών νοσημάτων δεν μπορεί να γίνεται αποσπασματικά, αλλά απαιτεί συνεργασία διαφορετικών ειδικοτήτων και συνολική προσέγγιση του ασθενούς. Ειδήσεις σήμερα «Πρώτες Βοήθειες για ζώα συντροφιάς» από τον Ελληνικό Ερυθρό Σταυρό ΙΣΑ: Υποτροφίες 70.000 ευρώ σε πρωτοετείς φοιτητές Ιατρικής – Ποιοι οι δικαιούχοι «Μια νότα, μια Φλόγα και χίλιες φωνές»: Μεγάλη μουσική βραδιά για τα παιδιά με καρκίνο

items.description: Η βιομηχανία εξόρυξης στρέφεται προς τον εξοπλισμό που λειτουργεί με μπαταρίες για να βελτιώσει την απόδοση, αλλά οι μπαταρίες ιόντων λιθίου ενέχουν κινδύνους λόγω της υψηλής ενεργειακής τους πυκνότητας. Μπορεί να αστοχήσουν, να υπερθερμανθούν και, σε ορισμένες περιπτώσεις, να πάρουν φωτιά, απελευθερώνοντας τοξικές εκπομπές.
items.descriptionOriginal: The mining industry is shifting toward battery-powered equipment to improve efficiency, but lithium-ion batteries pose risks due to their high energy density. They can fail, overheat and, in some cases, catch fire, releasing toxic emissions.

items.descriptionOriginal: Η Ισπανία θρηνεί τα θύματα της σιδηροδρομικής τραγωδίας στην επαρχία του Τολέδο , όπου τουλάχιστον 69 άνθρωποι έχασαν τη ζωή τους. Ανάμεσα στους τραυματίες που προσπαθούν να συνέλθουν από το σοκ βρίσκονται και τα μέλη μιας ελληνικής οικογένειας, η οποία είδε τις διακοπές της να μετατρέπονται σε εφιάλτη. Η μητέρα, μαζί με τους γιους της, τον 21χρονο Μάριο και τον 18χρονο Χρήστο, έφτασε αεροπορικώς στη Μαδρίτη το περασμένο Σάββατο (24/10) με προορισμό τη Σεβίλλη. Όπως περιγράφει η ισπανική εφημερίδα El Pais , η μητέρα τραυματίστηκε στην κλείδα και είναι καθηλωμένη σε αναπηρικό αμαξίδιο. «Είμαι ακόμη σε κατάσταση σοκ», δηλώνει χαρακτηριστικά. Λίγο πριν από τη σύγκρουση, η οικογένεια είχε χωριστεί. Ο Μάριος και η μητέρα του βρίσκονταν στο βαγόνι-εστιατόριο για πρωινό. Τη στιγμή που ετοιμάζονταν να παραλάβουν την παραγγελία τους, εκσφενδονίστηκαν από τη σφοδρή πρόσκρουση. «Ξαφνικά, ο χρόνος σταμάτησε», περιγράφει ο Μάριος. Το βαγόνι εκτροχιάστηκε, πήρε κλίση 30 μοιρών και γέμισε με μια έντονη μυρωδιά χώματος, ενώ για δευτερόλεπτα ακουγόταν ένας διαπεραστικός, άγριος ήχος. Παράλληλα, ο 18χρονος Χρήστος σώθηκε από καθαρή τύχη. Λίγο πριν από το δυστύχημα, είχε μετακινηθεί σε άλλο κάθισμα, καθώς η αρχική του θέση καταστράφηκε ολοσχερώς. Τα τρία μέλη κατάφεραν να επικοινωνήσουν τηλεφωνικά, να συναντηθούν και να βγουν έξω από το τρένο, αναζητώντας καταφύγιο σε ένα κοντινό χωράφι με αμυγδαλιές. Η οικογένεια εξέφρασε την ευγνωμοσύνη της για την αλληλεγγύη των ντόπιων. Ένας εθελοντής μάλιστα τους μετέφερε με το αυτοκίνητό του μακριά από τον τόπο της τραγωδίας προτού διακομιστούν στο νοσοκομείο. Μετά από αυτή την τραυματική εμπειρία, η οικογένεια ακύρωσε το ταξίδι της στη Σεβίλλη και σχεδιάζει την επιστροφή της αρχικά στη Μαδρίτη, και στη συνέχεια στην Ελλάδα.
